dedupe_keys.name: bgs and national grid transco rapid geohazard assessment of the uk gas transmission pipeline network

description: The British Geological Survey and National Grid Transco built a GIS for rapid assessment of whether a significant geohazard could affect any section of the UK natural gas transmission network, presented at the Geoline 2005 symposium in Lyon. National Grid Transco was responsible for the safety of the 18,000 km high-pressure network and, under health and safety legislation, had to show that risks to people near pipelines are managed, so it commissioned BGS, the main holder of national geological hazard data, to design GIS layers for its risk method. Landsliding and dissolution of soluble rocks were judged the greatest threats to the operating network, while clay shrinkage, running sand and compressible ground mattered mainly during construction. BGS national landslide and dissolution hazard datasets were clipped to buffer zones along the pipelines and enhanced with the National Landslide Database and the Karst Database, giving continuous layers of potential hazard at any point on the network. National Grid planned to use them to improve its risk method, inform discussions with the safety regulator and target surveillance. Coverage: Great Britain. Access: an open paper. Licence and cost: free. Caveats: a 2005 description; the GIS layers themselves are not public. It informs hazard exposure and resilience assessment of pipelines. It relates to the ALA buried pipeline fragility formulations and the US landslide exposure database in the catalogue.
